doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Playing styles, cruises and tribute bands
title: Cruise ship work with Dom DeLuise and as house drummer
summary: Going out with a celebrity is pleasant, house cruise work is poorly paid, and six months at sea destroys a network.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: No. Not unless your legs are not the same length or something. Tell me about playing on the — doing the cruise work. I’ve often wondered what exactly that is like.

Well it can — if you go out with an individual, I went out with Dom DeLuise once, an excellent comedian with eight pounds of music by the way, he sings, he dances, which there’s a side of him you don’t see. He sings opera and you have to know how to play these things. And going on with a celebrity is different than being the house drummer shall we say. We got Class A rooms, and we just played the show, which left plenty of time to go ashore and plenty of time to eat, and those cruises with him were very memorable and relaxing. We had great food, great people always great people on the band, and a wonderful, excellent personality, fun. Never stopped laughing. Practical joker. Those are fun. Being the house drummer is different nowadays because you have to wear a uniform, you have to help with shuffleboard during the day now, and you have what they call crew quarters, which are below the water line, and are not the most comfortable. And pay is not that great because they like to go after players and say well here is a paid vacation. Here’s pocket money and you’re going to see the world.

Yeah, students will come to me and say hey I got a call for a cruise. And I say wait a minute, let’s talk about this. And really being on a cruise for six months destroys any network that you’ve built, because you’re out of the music business, you’re out of contact.
You can’t even take like phone calls for work six months from then.
It destroys a network. Shore cruises are fine, two weeks or something like that are fine, and going out with a celebrity is the best because you get the excellent treatment, which you deserve.
